ClientPreference.description: One row per calling client: which providers it wants, per topic, best first. clientId is the X-Client-Id value; the reserved id 'default' is the fallback ladder, and the per-topic merge is the DSS's job, not this registry's. additionalProperties stays true -- a PUT re-validates the merged document carrying the registry's own os* fields, and false would reject every update (the SchemaRegistry.json defect).

clientId.description: The caller's name for itself, as sent in X-Client-Id. 'default' is reserved for the fallback ladder.

name.description: Display name for an operator reading the row, never matched against anything.

preferences.description: At least one topic. uniqueItems compares whole objects, so it cannot pin one entry per topic -- whoever writes rows checks that, the way verify/records.py does for ProviderSchema actions.

TopicRanking.description: One topic's ordered providers. Rank is array order, and the list is exclusive -- an unnamed provider is never consulted for the topic (DSS ADR-0019). topic is an open string on purpose: the DSS validates it against its own taxonomy, so a new topic needs no registry change.

topic.description: The ask's subject category as the consumer names it -- 'Weather', 'Market'. Compared case-insensitively by the reader, so casing here is cosmetic.

providers.description: Participant ids as the registry publishes them, best first. Unique, because a provider has one position in a ranking.
